mainTopic: Aggadic teachings on פסוקים (ישעיה, למנצח, יחזקאל), the journey of יוסף's treasure, קרח's wealth, and the speakers of the closing verses of הלל
overview: This amud opens by finishing the גמרא's reading of the פסוק in ישעיה about 'those who sit before ה'' and 'למכסה עתיק'. The person who sits before ה' is someone who is in the ישיבה so often that he knows his friend's seat or greets his friend there. 'למכסה עתיק' is read two ways: hiding סתרי תורה, or revealing טעמי תורה. Next come teachings in the name of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. The first says 'למנצח' praises God, who is happy when משה 'defeats' Him to save the Jews. The second says God's hand is spread under the wings of the חיות to receive בעלי תשובה. שמואל then traces the world's silver and gold from יוסף in מצרים, out with the Jews, and through many kings and empires until it reaches רומי. רבי חמא בר חנינא adds that יוסף hid three treasures, and the גמרא describes קרח's enormous wealth, which harmed him. The גמרא then returns to הלל and assigns each verse from אודך to the end of תהלים קיח to דוד, ישי, דוד's brothers, שמואל, or all of them together. Finally it begins quoting a משנה from סוכה about local custom in saying הלל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One who knows his friend's seat in the ישיבה
steps.stepSummary: The person called 'יושבים לפני ה'' is someone who knows where his friend sits in the ישיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is one who recognizes his friend's place in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the words 'ליושבים לפני ה'' (those who sit before ה'). It says this means a person who knows where his friend sits in the ישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This amud begins in the middle of a running explanation of the פסוק. Someone who knows everyone's seat must be in the ישיבה very often. Being there that regularly is what earns him the title 'sitting before ה''.

keyTerms.meaning: study hall, the place of Torah learning

phrases.english: This is one who recognizes his friend's place in the yeshiva.
phrases.notes: This explains 'ליושבים לפני ה'' from ישעיה 23:18, which was quoted on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the פסוק begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Sitting before ה'' means being in the ישיבה so regularly that you know everyone's seat.

steps.title: Second version: one who greets his friend in the ישיבה
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רבי אלעזר explained it as someone who greets his friend in the ישיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבי אלעזר said: This is one who greets his friend in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same explanation, said in the name of רבי אלעזר. 'Sitting before ה'' means someone who greets his friend in the ישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions describe a person who is always in the ישיבה. Here the sign of that is being there to greet a friend when he arrives. The basic idea stays the same; only the example changes.

keyTerms.meaning: some say; introduces a different version of a teaching
one who greets (literally, receives the face of)

phrases.english: Some say that Rabbi Elazar said:
This is one who greets his friend in the yeshiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the explanation in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, 'sitting before ה'' means being in the ישיבה to greet one's friend.

steps.title: What does 'stately clothing' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the next words of the פסוק, 'למכסה עתיק', mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'למכסה עתיק'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the end of the same פסוק and asks what 'למכסה עתיק' means. This is a setup line that prepares the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of the words is 'for stately clothing'. However, the word מכסה also means 'covering', and עתיק can hint to God, who is called 'עתיק יומין'. The question opens the door to a reading about hidden Torah knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: for stately clothing; read here as 'covering what the Ancient One hid'

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'limekhaseh atik'?
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of ישעיה 23:18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first part of the פסוק to its last words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the words 'למכסה עתיק'.

steps.title: One who keeps hidden what God hid: the secrets of Torah
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: it is someone who keeps hidden what עתיק יומין hid, namely סתרי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is one who covers up matters that the Ancient of Days covered. And what are they? The secrets of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'למכסה עתיק' describes a person who keeps hidden the things God chose to hide. Those things are סתרי תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מכסה is read as 'one who covers', and עתיק as God, the 'Ancient of Days'. סתרי תורה refers to deep mystical topics such as מעשה בראשית and מעשה מרכבה. These are not supposed to be taught openly, so the person who keeps them hidden is praised.

keyTerms.meaning: the Ancient of Days, a name for God (from דניאל)
the hidden, mystical secrets of the Torah

phrases.english: This is one who covers matters
that the Ancient of Days (God) covered.
And what are they? The secrets of the Torah.
phrases.notes: This means mystical topics like מעשה בראשית and מעשה מרכבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַמְכַסֶּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁכִּיסָּה עַתִּיק יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'למכסה עתיק' is someone who keeps hidden the סתרי תורה that God hid.

steps.title: Second version: one who reveals what God hid, the reasons of Torah
steps.stepSummary: Another version: it is someone who reveals what עתיק יומין hid, namely טעמי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: This is one who reveals matters that the Ancient of Days covered. What are they? The reasons of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an opposite reading. The person who is praised is the one who reveals what God hid, and those hidden things are the reasons behind the מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here מכסה is read as describing what God covered, not what the person does. The person earns reward by uncovering it. The hidden material changes from סתרי תורה, which should stay hidden, to טעמי תורה, the reasons behind the מצוות. The Torah did not state these reasons openly, and this reading praises the one who reveals them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. The first view praises HIDING סתרי תורה. The second view praises REVEALING טעמי תורה. These are different topics, not one topic treated two ways. Some English translations add that these reasons 'should be kept secret'. That gloss does not match this view, which praises the one who reveals them.
steps.whatToRemember: 'למכסה עתיק' has two readings. One is keeping hidden what God hid (סתרי תורה). The other is revealing what God hid (טעמי תורה).

phrases.english: And some say: This is one who reveals matters
that the Ancient of Days covered.
What are they? The reasons of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: זֶה הַמְגַלֶּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁכִּיסָּה עַתִּיק יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of the answer in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'למכסה עתיק' is someone who reveals the טעמי תורה that God hid.

steps.title: 'למנצח': sing to the One who is happy when defeated
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא, quoting רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, reads 'למנצח' as 'sing to the One who is happy when they defeat Him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי: What is the meaning of what is written, 'למנצח מזמור לדוד'? Sing to the One whom people defeat, and He is happy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רב כהנא in the name of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. He explains the word 'למנצח' at the start of many chapters of תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word למנצח comes from the root נצח, which means 'to win'. He reads it as describing God, whom people can 'defeat' and who is glad when they do. The proof comes in the following steps.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written?
'to the conductor'; read here from נצח, to win

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:
What is the meaning of what is written: 'Lamenatzeach, a psalm of David'?
Sing to the One whom they defeat, and He is happy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new aggadic teaching in the name of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, a תנא whose teachings are being collected here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'למנצח' means: sing to God, who is happy when people 'defeat' Him.

steps.title: God is unlike people: defeat makes Him happy
steps.stepSummary: The teaching continues: a human being is sad when defeated, but הקדוש ברוך הוא is happy when defeated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see that the way of בשר ודם is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. A person of בשר ודם is defeated and becomes sad, but הקדוש ברוך הוא is defeated and is happy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expands the point by comparing God to people. When people lose, they feel sad. When God 'loses', He is happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step spells out how unusual it is to be happy about losing. The contrast between בשר ודם and הקדוש ברוך הוא makes it clear. It also sets up the need for a פסוק that shows God being 'defeated'.

keyTerms.meaning: flesh and blood, a human being

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that unlike the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
Flesh and blood: they defeat him and he is sad,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא — נוֹצְחִין אוֹתוֹ וְשָׂמֵחַ,
phrases.english: but the Holy One, Blessed be He: they defeat Him and He is happy,

steps.triggerLanguage: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the idea from step 6 by comparing God to human beings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humans are sad when defeated, while God is happy when defeated.

steps.title: Proof from משה standing in the breach
steps.stepSummary: The proof: God wanted to destroy the Jews, משה stopped Him, and the פסוק still calls משה 'His chosen one'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And He said He would destroy them, had not משה His chosen one stood in the breach before Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from תהלים (106:23) to prove that God is happy when He is 'defeated'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God said He would destroy the Jewish people, and משה stood against that and 'won'. Even so, the פסוק calls משה 'בחירו', His chosen one. This shows God was pleased that משה defeated Him.

keyTerms.meaning: had not, were it not for

steps.whatToRemember: God is happy when a צדיק 'defeats' Him to save the Jewish people. That is why משה is still called 'His chosen one'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows that sincere תפילה that pleads for mercy, even against a harsh decree, is something God welcomes.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And He said He would destroy them,'
had not Moshe His chosen one
stood in the breach before Him.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to prove the claim made in steps 6 and 7.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that God is happy when people 'defeat' Him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 106:23: משה prevented the destruction and is still called 'בחירו'.

steps.title: A new teaching opens on a verse about the angels' hands
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a chain of tradition going back to רבי יהודה נשיאה. He asks what the פסוק in יחזקאל means by 'the hands of a man under their wings.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש, in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: What does the verse mean, 'And the hands of a man were under their wings'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new aggadic teaching and quotes a פסוק from יחזקאל's vision of the חיות. This line is a setup: the explanation comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מאי דכתיב' tells us the speaker sees something unusual in the verse that needs explaining. The verse describes the angels who carry the Divine chariot. The chain of names shows that this teaching was handed down carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
Their wings (the wings of the חיות)
The Nasi (title of רבי יהודה, a grandson of רבי)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And the hands of a man under their wings"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל א:ח, describing the חיות of the מרכבה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic teaching from the same speaker, רב כהנא. It continues the theme of God's kindness to His creations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This teaching, completed in step 10, reads the 'hands of a man' under the wings of the חיות as a hint to God's own hand.

steps.title: It is God's hand, spread out to receive people doing תשובה
steps.stepSummary: The word is written 'his hand' (singular). So it refers to the hand of הקדוש ברוך הוא, spread under the wings to receive בעלי תשובה and protect them from מדת הדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word is written 'his hand.' This is the hand of הקדוש ברוך הוא, which is spread out under the wings of the חיות to receive people doing תשובה and save them from the attribute of strict justice.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer points to the spelling of the word. It is read 'hands' but written 'his hand,' and so it hints at God's own hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way a word is written in תנ״ך (the כתיב) can differ from the way it is read (the קרי). Here the written form, singular 'his hand,' teaches a hidden idea: God Himself reaches out to receive those who repent. Strict justice might block a sinner from returning, but God's hand protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (the spelling, as opposed to how the word is read)

steps.whatToRemember: God's hand is spread out to receive בעלי תשובה, even when מדת הדין would push them away.

phrases.english: "His hand" is written
phrases.notes: The word is read וִידֵי (hands) but written ידו (his hand)

phrases.aramaic: זֶה יָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: this is the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He
that is spread out under the wings of the חיות
in order to receive penitents
from the hand of the attribute of justice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 9 by pointing to how the word is written.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular spelling 'his hand' refers to God's hand, which receives בעלי תשובה and shields them from מדת הדין.

steps.title: יוסף gathered all the world's silver and gold into מצרים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that יוסף collected all the silver and gold in the world and brought it to מצרים. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: All the silver and gold in the world, יוסף gathered it and brought it to מצרים, as it says, 'And יוסף gathered all the money that was found.'
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new teaching begins about where the world's wealth went. שמואל claims יוסף gathered all of it into מצרים, and quotes a פסוק to support this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'all the money that was found.' שמואל reads 'all' as truly including everything. The next steps check whether the verse really covers every land.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (a verse is coming)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
All the silver and gold in the world
Joseph gathered it and brought it to Egypt,
as it is said:
"And Joseph gathered all the money that was found."
phrases.notes: בראשית מז:יד. The verse continues 'in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An unrelated new aggadic teaching. It is not connected to step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף gathered all the world's silver and gold into מצרים.

steps.title: What about money from other countries?
steps.stepSummary: The verse mentions only מצרים and כנען. So how do we know יוסף gathered the money of the other lands too?
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about the money in the land of מצרים and the land of כנען. How do I know about other lands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap. The full verse names only מצרים and כנען, so it does not yet prove that 'all the world's' money went to מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל claimed יוסף gathered the money of the whole world. The proof verse, read in full, limits itself to two lands. A second source is needed for every other country.

phrases.english: I have only that which was in the land of Egypt
and that which was in the land of Canaan;
from where do we know about other lands?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the proof verse in step 11 covers only two lands.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the money of all other lands also came to מצרים.

steps.title: All the lands came to מצרים
steps.stepSummary: A second verse says the whole world came to מצרים to buy food. So their money ended up there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'And all the land came to מצרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another פסוק. It says all the lands came to מצרים to buy food from יוסף during the famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every country came to buy grain from יוסף, every country paid him. This fills the gap from step 12 and proves שמואל's claim that the whole world's wealth reached מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a proof verse)

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And all the land came to Egypt."
phrases.notes: בראשית מא:נז. They came to buy grain from יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a second verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since all lands came to מצרים to buy food, their money went there too.

steps.title: The Jews took the treasure out of מצרים
steps.stepSummary: When כלל ישראל left מצרים, they took all this wealth with them. The source is the verse 'וינצלו את מצרים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And when ישראל went up from מצרים, they took it up with them, as it says: 'And they emptied out מצרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל's history continues: the wealth gathered by יוסף left מצרים with the Jews. This sets up the next two steps, which explain the word 'וינצלו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treasure moves from מצרים into the hands of כלל ישראל. The verb 'וינצלו' is unusual, so two אמוראים will each explain how fully מצרים was emptied.

phrases.english: And when Israel went up from Egypt
they brought it up with them,
as it is said: "And they emptied out Egypt."
phrases.notes: שמות יב:לו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's story: the treasure now leaves מצרים with כלל ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלל ישראל took all of יוסף's gathered wealth out of מצרים.

steps.title: רב אסי: מצרים became like a trap with no grain
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי reads 'וינצלו' as related to מצודה, a bird trap. They left מצרים like a trap with no grain bait left in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: They made it like this trap that has no grain in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי explains the word 'וינצלו' with a picture. A bird trap normally has grain in it as bait, and מצרים was left like a trap with none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that מצרים was left completely empty of its wealth. רב אסי connects the word to מצודה (trap) and the image of missing grain.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
They made it like this trap
that has no grain in it,
phrases.notes: Grain is normally placed in a trap as bait

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'וינצלו' from the verse quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וינצלו means they left מצרים empty, like a trap without grain.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: מצרים became like deep water with no fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads 'וינצלו' as related to מצולה, the depths of the sea. They left מצרים like deep water with no fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Like the depths of the sea that have no fish in them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a second picture for the same word. מצרים was left like the depths of the sea with no fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that מצרים was totally emptied. They differ only in which word they hear inside 'וינצלו': מצודה (trap) or מצולה (depths).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two images. רב אסי says מצודה (a trap) without דגן (grain). רבי שמעון says מצולה (the deep sea) without דגים (fish). The words sound alike, but both mean the same thing: מצרים was left empty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Like the depths of the sea that have no fish in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different picture from רב אסי's for the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וינצלו means they left מצרים empty, like the deep sea without fish.

steps.title: The treasure stayed until רחבעם, then שישק took it
steps.stepSummary: The wealth stayed with כלל ישראל until the days of רחבעם. Then שישק king of מצרים came and took it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it remained until רחבעם. Then שישק king of מצרים came and took it from רחבעם.
steps.whatsHappening: The history moves forward many generations. The treasure that left מצרים now goes back to a king of מצרים, and the next step brings the proof verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treasure stayed with כלל ישראל from יציאת מצרים until the son of שלמה. Under רחבעם it was lost back to מצרים.

phrases.english: And it remained until Rehoboam.
Shishak king of Egypt came
and took it from Rehoboam,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the treasure's journey after יציאת מצרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The treasure stayed in ישראל until רחבעם, when שישק took it.

steps.title: The verse about שישק taking the treasures
steps.stepSummary: The verse in מלכים says שישק came up against ירושלים in רחבעם's fifth year. He took the treasures of the בית המקדש and of the king's palace.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And it was in the fifth year of King רחבעם, שישק king of מצרים came up against ירושלים, and took the treasures of the House of ה' and the treasures of the king's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse to prove that שישק took the treasure from רחבעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says שישק took both the Temple treasury and the royal treasury. This matches the claim that the great treasure from מצרים passed to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The House of ה׳ (the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: as it is said:
"And it was in the fifth year of King Rehoboam
Shishak king of Egypt came up [against Jerusalem]
and he took the treasures of the House of the Lord
and the treasures of the king's house."
phrases.notes: מלכים א יד:כה-כו

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיְהִי בַּשָּׁנָה הַחֲמִישִׁית לַמֶּלֶךְ רְחַבְעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 17 with a verse.
steps.raayaObject: That שישק took the treasure from רחבעם.

steps.title: זרח king of כוש took it from שישק
steps.stepSummary: The treasure changed hands again: זרח king of כוש took it from שישק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then זרח king of כוש came and took it from שישק.
steps.whatsHappening: The chain of owners continues: after שישק, זרח king of כוש took the treasure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treasure keeps passing from one ruler to the next. This shows that worldly wealth never stays with any one owner for long.

phrases.english: Zerah king of Kush came
and took it from Shishak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next link in the treasure's chain after שישק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זרח king of כוש took the treasure from שישק.

steps.title: The treasure passes from אסא to יהושפט
steps.stepSummary: אסא took the treasure from זרח and sent it to הדרימון בן טברימון. בני עמון took it from him. Then יהושפט took it back, and it stayed until אחז.
steps.simpleTranslation: אסא came and took it from זרח king of כוש, and sent it to הדרימון בן טברימון. בני עמון came and took it from הדרימון בן טברימון. יהושפט came and took it from בני עמון, and it stayed in place until אחז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps following the chain of owners of the treasure from מצרים, picking up where step 19 stopped with זרח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each link is the same pattern: someone 'came and took it' from the one before. The treasure goes from כוש back to a Jewish king, אסא, then out to ארם and עמון, and then back to a Jewish king, יהושפט. It then stays put for a while, until the days of אחז.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of יהודה who defeated זרח

phrases.english: Asa came and took it
from Zerah, king of Kush
phrases.notes: After defeating him in battle (דברי הימים ב יד)

phrases.english: and sent it to Hadrimmon ben Tabrimmon.
phrases.notes: The king of ארם (see מלכים א טו)

phrases.english: The children of Ammon came and took them
from Hadrimmon ben Tabrimmon.
Jehoshaphat came and took it from the children of Ammon
and it remained until Ahaz.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא אָסָא וּנְטָלוֹ מִזֶּרַח מֶלֶךְ כּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of owners right after זרח took it from שישק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The treasure went from זרח to אסא, then to הדרימון, then to בני עמון, then to יהושפט, where it stayed until אחז.

steps.title: The treasure travels from אחז all the way to רומי
steps.stepSummary: סנחריב took it from אחז, חזקיה took it back, and it stayed until צדקיה. Then the כשדים, the Persians, the Greeks, and the Romans each took it in turn. It is still in רומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: סנחריב came and took it from אחז. חזקיה came and took it from סנחריב, and it stayed until צדקיה. The כשדים came and took it from צדקיה. The Persians took it from the כשדים. The Greeks took it from the Persians. The Romans took it from the Greeks, and it is still resting in רומי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain of owners, ending with the Romans, who still have the treasure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After חזקיה, the treasure never comes back to כלל ישראל. It moves through the great empires one after another: בבל (the כשדים), פרס, יון, and רומי. The final words, 'and it is still resting in רומי,' close the story in the time of the גמרא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: King of אשור who attacked יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: The treasure from מצרים passed through many hands: Jewish kings sometimes won it back, but in the end the great empires took it, and it is still in רומי.

phrases.english: Sennacherib came and took it from Ahaz.
Hezekiah came and took it from Sennacherib
and it remained until Zedekiah.
The Chaldeans came and took it from Zedekiah.
The Persians came and took it from the Chaldeans.
The Greeks came and took it from the Persians.
The Romans came and took it from the hand of the Greeks,
and it still remains in Rome.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same chain from אחז and brings it to its end in רומי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The treasure passed through סנחריב, חזקיה, the כשדים, Persians, and Greeks, and is now in רומי.

steps.title: יוסף hid three treasures in מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא says יוסף hid three treasures in מצרים. One was found by קרח, one by אנטונינוס, and one is saved for the צדיקים in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: יוסף hid three treasures in מצרים. One was revealed to קרח, one was revealed to אנטונינוס בן אסוירוס, and one is stored away for the צדיקים in the future to come.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of the wealth of מצרים, the גמרא brings a new teaching about three treasures that יוסף hid there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף collected huge wealth in מצרים during the famine. This teaching says it was hidden in three places with three different fates. The mention of קרח sets up the next steps, which talk about קרח's wealth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said:
Joseph hid three treasures in Egypt,
one was revealed to Korah,
and one was revealed to Antoninos ben Asveiros,
phrases.notes: A Roman emperor

phrases.english: and one is hidden for the righteous in the future to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא שָׁלֹשׁ מַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת הִטְמִין יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the treasure that left מצרים with כלל ישראל to treasures יוסף hid in מצרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף hid three treasures: one found by קרח, one by אנטונינוס, and one saved for the צדיקים.

steps.title: Riches kept to his hurt means קרח's wealth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the verse 'riches kept by its owner to his hurt' refers to קרח's wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Riches kept by its owner to his hurt.' רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: This is the wealth of קרח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now focuses on the first treasure, the one קרח found. ריש לקיש says a verse in קהלת is talking about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in קהלת speaks of wealth that ends up harming its owner. ריש לקיש says קרח is the example: his wealth made him proud, which led to his rebellion and his downfall.

phrases.english: 'Riches kept by its owner to his hurt' (Ecclesiastes 5:12),
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
This is the wealth of Korah.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹשֶׁר שָׁמוּר לִבְעָלָיו לְרָעָתוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the treasure that step 22 said was revealed to קרח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'riches kept to his hurt' in קהלת are קרח's wealth.

steps.title: A person's money stands him on his feet
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the verse about the property 'at their feet' that the earth swallowed, רבי אלעזר says this means a person's money, which stands him on his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the verse says: 'And all the substance that was at their feet.' רבי אלעזר said: This is a person's money, which stands him up on his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse about the earth swallowing קרח's group along with their property, and רבי אלעזר explains the odd phrase 'at their feet.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have just said 'their property.' רבי אלעזר says 'at their feet' teaches that money is what lets a person stand on his own feet, meaning it supports him. The verse also shows that קרח's group lost their wealth when the earth swallowed them, which fits 'riches kept to his hurt.'

phrases.english: (As it is stated:) 'And all the substance that was at their feet' (Deuteronomy 11:6),
phrases.notes: The verse is about the earth swallowing the rebels and their belongings

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This is a person's money
that stands him upon his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְאֶת כׇּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶם אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a verse showing that קרח's group lost their wealth, and explains its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The substance at their feet' means a person's money, which keeps him standing.

steps.title: קרח's treasury keys filled 300 mules
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says the keys to קרח's treasure houses were a load for 300 white mules, even though they were made of light leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: The keys to קרח's treasure houses were a load for three hundred white mules, and all of them were keys and locks made of leather.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי describes just how enormous קרח's wealth was, by describing the size of his keys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather keys and locks are very light. If even the light keys needed 300 mules to carry them, then the number of treasure rooms must have been huge. This shows how great the wealth was that later led to קרח's downfall.

keyTerms.meaning: A load, a burden to carry

steps.whatToRemember: קרח's wealth, found from יוסף's hidden treasure, was huge. Even his light leather keys needed 300 mules. Yet that wealth was 'kept to his hurt' and was swallowed with him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
A load for three hundred white mules

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ מַפְתְּחוֹת בֵּית גְּנָזָיו שֶׁל קֹרַח,
phrases.english: were the keys of Korah's treasure houses,
and all of them were keys and locks of leather.
phrases.notes: Leather is light, which makes the huge load even more striking

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי מַשּׂאוֹי שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת פְּרָדוֹת לְבָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a picture of how large קרח's wealth was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח's treasury keys, though made of light leather, were a load for 300 white mules.

steps.title: Who said the first four verses starting from אודך
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן assigns פסוקים כא–כד of תהלים קיח to four speakers: דוד, ישי, דוד's brothers, and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: דיא״ש אדי״ש כשד״ך מאוד״ך.) רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: "I will thank You, for You answered me" was said by דוד. "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone" was said by ישי. "This is from ה׳" was said by his brothers. "This is the day ה׳ has made" was said by שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a סימן (memory sign), then begins a teaching that splits the closing verses of הלל among different people, as if they were speaking in turn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The background is the day שמואל came to ישי's house and anointed the youngest son, דוד (שמואל א טז). דוד thanks ה׳ for answering him. ישי calls his overlooked son the "rejected stone" that became the cornerstone. The brothers say this is ה׳'s doing, and שמואל declares it a day ה׳ made. The letters of the first word of the סימן, דיא״ש, stand for דוד, ישי, אחיו, שמואל, the order of speakers in this step.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign: letters that help you remember the order of a passage
"I will thank You, for You answered me" (תהלים קיח:כא)
"The stone the builders rejected": here, דוד, whom others overlooked
Cornerstone, the most important stone in a building

steps.confusionAlert: In this passage שמואל means שמואל הנביא, the prophet who anointed דוד. He is not the אמורא שמואל, and he is not רבי שמואל בר נחמני, who is reporting the teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because each verse from אודך onward has a separate speaker, each one stands as its own statement. This connects to the custom of saying each of these verses twice in הלל, which the next discussion about local custom touches on.

phrases.english: (Dalet-Yud-Aleph-Shin, Aleph-Dalet-Yud-Shin, Kaf-Shin-Dalet-Kaf, Me'odcha: a memory sign).
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for a speaker: ד = דוד, י = ישי, א = אחיו, ש = שמואל, כ = כולן (all of them). מאוד״ך is usually taken as a hint that it all starts from "אודך."

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
"I will thank You, for You answered me": David said this.
phrases.notes: דוד thanks ה׳ for being chosen.

phrases.english: "The stone that the builders rejected
has become the cornerstone": Yishai said this.
phrases.notes: ישי had not even brought דוד in to meet שמואל at first.

phrases.english: "This is from ה׳": his brothers said this.
"This is the day ה׳ has made": Samuel said this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the aggadic side discussions on this amud, including the treasures and קרח's wealth (steps 11–25), the גמרא returns to explaining the verses of הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verses of תהלים קיח from אודך onward were spoken by different people on the day דוד was anointed: verse 21 by דוד, 22 by ישי, 23 by his brothers, 24 by שמואל.

steps.title: Who said the remaining verses until the end of the chapter
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching continues, assigning פסוקים כה–כח to the brothers, דוד, ישי, שמואל, and all of them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Please ה׳, save us" was said by his brothers. "Please ה׳, make us succeed" was said by דוד. "Blessed is the one who comes in the name of ה׳" was said by ישי. "We bless you from the house of ה׳" was said by שמואל. "ה׳ is God, and He gave us light" was said by all of them. "Bind the festival offering with ropes" was said by שמואל. "You are my God and I will thank You" was said by דוד. "My God, I will exalt You" was said by all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same list of speakers through the last verses of the chapter. Some verses are said by one person and some by everyone together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a single verse can be split in two. Verse 25 is divided between the brothers ("הושיעה נא") and דוד ("הצליחה נא"), and verse 28 between דוד and everyone. The second and third words of the סימן match this step. אדי״ש means אחיו, דוד, ישי, שמואל, and כשד״ך means כולן, שמואל, דוד, כולן.

keyTerms.meaning: "Bind the festival offering with ropes": prepare the celebration offering

steps.whatToRemember: From אודך to the end of תהלים קיח, each verse, and sometimes each half-verse, has its own speaker from the scene of דוד's anointing. The סימן דיא״ש אדי״ש כשד״ך lists them in order.

phrases.english: "Please, ה׳, save us": his brothers said this.
"Please, ה׳, make us succeed": David said this.
"Blessed is the one who comes in the name of ה׳": Yishai said this.
"We bless you from the house of ה׳": Samuel said this.
"ה׳ is God, and He gave us light": all of them said this.
"Bind the festival offering with ropes": Samuel said this.
"You are my God, and I will thank You": David said this.
"My God, I will exalt You": all of them said this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָנָּא ה׳ הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא — אָמְרוּ אֶחָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly continues the same teaching of רבי שמואל בר נחמני from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Verses 25–28 are split as follows: brothers, דוד, ישי, שמואל, all together, שמואל, דוד, all together.

steps.title: Quoting a משנה about local custom in saying הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה from מסכת סוכה that opens with "in a place where they were accustomed."
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there (in מסכת סוכה): "In a place where they were accustomed..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts quoting a משנה from another מסכת, and the full quote and discussion continue in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תנן התם" tells us the source is a משנה found elsewhere, here in סוכה. That משנה teaches that people should follow local custom in how they say הלל, for example whether to repeat certain verses. This connects naturally to the verses just discussed, which many communities say twice.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learned there": a משנה from a different מסכת is being quoted
"A place where they were accustomed": the opening of a rule about local custom

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a משנה of פסחים. "התם" (there) means the quote comes from a different מסכת, here סוכה.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishnah): In a place where they were accustomed
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the aggadic reading of הלל's verses to a halachic source about local customs in reciting הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a משנה from סוכה that makes the practice of reciting הלל depend on local custom. The ruling itself is completed on the next amud.
